data.name: Kutumbini
data.gender_notes: Kutumbini is used as a unisex name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Kutumbini is a Sanskrit name derived from the word 'kutumba', which means 'family'. Kutumbini is the goddess of the family, protectress of the home, and giver of prosperity and happiness. She is invoked to ensure the well-being and harmony of the family. The name Kutumbini carries the meaning “Goddess of the family” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Kutumbini usually hope their child will grow to embody goddess of the family and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Protector of the family, giver of happiness and prosperity
data.etymology: Kutumbini belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Goddess of the family.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kutumbini total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

data.cultural_impact: In Hindu culture, the family is a fundamental unit of society. The traditional Hindu joint family system is deeply rooted in societal values and communal living. Kutumbini is the protective deity of this social unit, ensuring its stability and prosperity. At the individual level, she is invoked for the blessings of a peaceful, harmonious, and prosperous family life.
data.spiritual_significance: Spiritually, Kutumbini represents the essence of love, unity, and protection. She embodies the Hindu understanding of the family as a sacred institution, bonding individuals together in love and mutual support. Invoking her blessings, one seeks not just material prosperity, but spiritual growth and harmony within the familial unit.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Kutumbini represents the embodiment of family unity and bonding. The name signifies the power that binds the family together, invoking love, respect, and mutual support. It is the sacred force that keeps the Hindu joint family system thriving.

historical_references.reference: Kutumbini, also known as Goddess Saraswati, is believed to have been mentioned in the ancient Hindu sacred text, the Mahabharata, which is estimated to have been composed between 400 BCE and 200 CE.
historical_references.context: Mentioned as a goddess in the Mahabharata, an ancient Hindu text

historical_references.reference: Another reference suggests that Kutumbini was worshipped as a goddess of prosperity and fertility in the medieval period of India, particularly in the regions of Karnataka and Andhra Pradesh.
historical_references.context: Worshipped as a goddess of prosperity and fertility in the medieval period of India

trends: Preserver of family values and traditions
modern_usage.modern_context: The Hindu goddess Kutumbini, also known as Kutumba Devi or Parvati, is revered as the protector and preserver of family values, traditions, and unity. In Hindu mythology, she is depicted as a goddess who embodies the essence of family and prosperity. In modern contexts, Kutumbini is invoked and celebrated during Indian marriage ceremonies as a symbol of unity and togetherness. She is also honored during various Indian festivals, such as Diwali and Karwa Chauth, as a sign of respect for the importance and sanctity of the family unit.

name_in_real_life.story: A devoted individual named Radha Kutumbini in Delhi, India attributes much of their spiritual journey to their name Kutumbini, which means "Goddess of the family". They believe their name has guided them on the path of righteousness.
